metadata.case_name: LAM CHU v. TSE LUM WONG & ANOTHER

plaintiff.occupation_before: toll collector at the Shing Mun Tunnel

injuries.description: Post Concussional Syndrome / mild head injury
source: The plaintiff was knocked unconscious and suffered amnesia afterwards. She was unconscious for two hours. She was seen by three different experts. In short she suffered Post Concussional Syndrome as a result of the accident. The symptoms, which are ongoing, include headaches, impaired concentration, irritability and insomnia.
injuries.icd_description: Concussion with loss of consciousness, short duration of one hour to less than 6 hours

injuries.description: Fracture of the pelvis (with residual pain and limited mobility affecting left hip and buttock)
source: Her pelvis was fractured by the impact.

Dr David H.F. Cheng. She still complained of pelvis pain and said she could not stand or sit for more than 30 minutes without feeling pain. Dr Cheng reported that the fracture had healed but that residual pain continued.

In March 2003 she was seen by Dr Conrad Pei Kee Wai, a specialist physician, who opined that her condition was as a result of the accident. He said that her pelvic pain and limited mobility were likely to be permanent.
injuries.icd_description: Fracture of pelvic bone without disruption of posterior arch of pelvic ring

injuries.description: Facial and scalp lacerations and abrasions
injuries.body_part: forehead, head, nose, lip and chin
source: She sustained a one-cm cut to her forehead, a four-cm cut to her head and other abrasions to her head, nose, lip and chin.

injuries.description: Hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (diagnosed 23 July 2000) on hormone replacement therapy
source: On 23 July 2000 the plaintiff was diagnosed with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and put on hormone replacement therapy. In March 2003 she was seen by Dr Conrad Pei Kee Wai, a specialist physician, who opined that her condition was as a result of the accident.

injuries.description: Contused bladder with mild incontinence (resolved by 2003 with occasional urinary urgency)
source: She suffered a contused bladder as a result of the collision. Since the accident she has suffered mild incontinence. Examination in 2003 indicated that this was no longer a problem. The plaintiff however complained that occasional urinary urgency still occurred.

injuries.description: Depression / psychiatric condition (ongoing; requiring counselling and antidepressant medication)
source: Whilst her recovery from the accident continued to be slow she developed psychiatric problems. She worried about being unable to work, suffered from anxiety and insomnia and occasionally considered suicide. She required counselling and antidepressant medication.
There is general agreement that she suffers from depression due to the continuation of her pain, headaches and the cumulation of her other problems alluded to above.

manifestations.description: unconscious for two hours and amnesia afterwards
residual pelvic pain and inability to stand or sit for more than 30 minutes without pain
limited mobility; use of walking stick, walking frame and wheelchair at times
mild urinary incontinence (resolved by 2003) with occasional urinary urgency

treatments_received: use of walking stick, walking frame and wheelchair at times

losses.category: Loss of ability to do domestic tasks
losses.description: Unable to do household duties as part of the support for her mother; prevented from carrying out that support role for three years.
Use of walking stick, walking frame and wheelchair; cannot do prolonged walking; limited mobility continuing.
Impaired concentration and cognitive symptoms related to Post Concussional Syndrome.
Requires accompaniment when going out; does not go out unaccompanied.
Loss of job which she particularly enjoyed and which was of particular importance to her; loss of self-esteem from being unable to continue that employment.
